text: Thirty-nine thousand dollars, in an exporter's wallet, the day the goods ship. This is Hisab on Monad.
Small exporters wait ninety days to get paid. Here, a lender pool advances the cash instead. This is the live console on Monad testnet, with three roles and three wallets.
Wallets are burners by default. Or connect a browser wallet, or log in with email through Privy.
Exporter first. One click funds gas, registers a forty-eight thousand seven hundred fifty dollar shipping bill, and seeds two on-time invoices of history.
That history earns tier one: eighty percent advance, at twelve and a half percent. So the offer is thirty-nine thousand A U S D.
Now a lender. Mint some test A U S D, deposit a hundred thousand, and the pool mints shares against it.
Next, the buyer. They sign an E I P seven-twelve message. No signature, no financing.
Back to the exporter, who accepts the offer. The receivable locks to the pool, and thirty-nine thousand lands in the same transaction. Confirmed in about three seconds, end to end.
Try to finance the same bill twice, and the contract refuses. Double financing, blocked.
Now the buyer pays. One transaction, three legs. Forty thousand to the pool, principal plus interest. A twenty-six dollar fee. And eight thousand seven hundred twenty-two to the exporter.
Paid on time, so the exporter climbs to tier two: eighty-eight percent advance, at eleven and a half. Register the next invoice, and the offer jumps to forty-two thousand nine hundred.
And the lender? The share price ticked up. That is interest, earned from a real shipment.
Open the explorer. Every state links to its Monad transaction: registered, acknowledged, financed, paid.
Short pays are marked partial. A missed due date drops the exporter to tier zero. Twenty-eight contract tests pass, and the legacy SWIFT path is still there.
Why Monad? Fast finality. Every step you just saw confirmed in about three seconds. And A U S D is the single asset, a mock on testnet.
Hisab on Monad. Live now, code on GitHub. Built with Monad, A U S D, and Privy.
